import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
data = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')
data.head()

# Create a bar chart to compare the average price of cameras by sensor type
plt.figure(figsize=(8,6))
sns.barplot(x='sensor_type', y='price_usd', data=data)
plt.title('Average Price of Cameras by Sensor Type')
plt.xlabel('Sensor Type')
plt.ylabel('Average Price (USD)')
plt.xticks(rotation=45)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

# Create a histogram to show the distribution of megapixels
plt.figure(figsize=(8,6))
sns.histplot(data['megapixels'], kde=True)
plt.title('Distribution of Megapixels in Cameras')
plt.xlabel('Megapixels')
plt.ylabel('Frequency')
plt.xticks(rotation=45)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output2.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

# Create a scatter plot to show the relationship between weight and megapixels
plt.figure(figsize=(8,6))
sns.scatterplot(x='megapixels', y='weight_grams', data=data)
plt.title('Relationship between Camera Weight and Megapixels')
plt.xlabel('Megapixels')
plt.ylabel('Weight (grams)')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output3.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
